## About Me

I am a PhD candidate in Health Services Research,
specializing in health economics, at
Texas A&M University.

My research examines how healthcare regulation,
market structures, and public policies shape
organizational behavior, resource allocation,
and access to care. I am particularly interested
in how regulatory constraints and market
incentives influence the decisions and
performance of healthcare organizations.

My current research focuses on hospital
regulation, competition, and organizational
responses to policy changes. I use causal
inference and quasi-experimental methods,
including difference-in-differences and
synthetic control methods, to evaluate health
policies and their consequences for healthcare
organizations and communities.

Prior to my doctoral studies, I worked in
regulatory policy and intelligence at
Johnson & Johnson, Daiichi Sankyo, and
Medtronic. This professional experience
informs my broader interest in how regulatory
environments influence economic decisions
and organizational performance across
healthcare and life sciences.

## Research Interests

- Health Economics
- Healthcare Regulation and Competition
- Hospital Markets and Organizational Behavior
- Health Policy Evaluation
- Healthcare Access and Delivery
